Implemented on task/ravel-amn.2 (stacked on task/ravel-amn.1), PR to follow. New src/materialize.rs returns a typed MaterializedBase only after verifying the frozen commit, the frozen tree, and the sha256 of git archive output, extracting only after that digest matches. Fetch is a bare repo from an empty template with inherited environment cleared, system and global config disabled, prompts off, core.hooksPath=/dev/null and no checkout; the tree parser rejects non-blob types, modes other than 100644/100755, and .gitmodules / .gitattributes / .cargo/config* at any depth, so repository-supplied hooks, filters and attributes never act. MaterializedBase has no public path accessor, no Deref and no AsRef<Path>, and LaunchPaths::new now REQUIRES it, so amn.1's sandbox can no longer be handed a raw source path — that closes amn.1 residual R11 and makes launch-kind confusability compiler-enforced end to end. Design: spec-pipeline then two independent sign-off lanes, both SIGN OFF WITH CONDITIONS, folded in as binding amendments A1-A6. A1 OVERTURNED the spec's own plan to shell out to python3 for the collision key: a lane probe showed the frozen base tree is 66 entries, max 41 bytes, depth 3 and ZERO non-ASCII, so an ASCII-restricted Rust key equals the frozen key here and is strictly stricter in general, removing a subprocess, a hex protocol and the host unicodedata dependency from the trusted path; the 19 golden vectors were also shown unable to bound Unicode-version drift, since every vector input is assigned in Unicode 1.1 and reproduces identically on 15.1. Ruling recorded as e06-amn2-base-collision-key; the general key and its version ruling are deferred to ravel-amn.4 and noted there. A3 fixed a probe-demonstrated build break: cargo discovers configuration from cwd upward, so a host-side cargo invocation inside the snapshot picks up the trusted .cargo/config.toml whose target-dir and vendor directory are in-sandbox paths; every host cargo call now runs with cwd outside the snapshot and --manifest-path pointing in. A4 ruled the first Git effect EXCLUDED BY RULING rather than gated (a fetch is a read, the result is pinned by three frozen values, there is no third-party spend, and gating is operationally impossible because materialization precedes host isolation and any claim, so no authority exists to consume) and e06-effect-gate-taxonomy was amended accordingly: Git moved out of GENUINELY ABSENT into entry 5, leaving only the code host absent. Review: wave 1 (rust-code-reviewer 0 blocking, security-reviewer 0 blocking, invariant-test-review 2 blocking) found that the ENTIRE AC3 tree preflight was unwired-detectable — replacing the validate_tree call with a no-op left all offline tests green because the parser was proven only in isolation — and that A2's mandated materialized-tree ASCII assertion was vacuous against an all-ASCII fixture; also that the permission guard survived four mutations (mask narrowed to 0o002 or 0o020, symlink_metadata to metadata, and dropping the directory recursion). Both fixed with mutation proofs: unwiring validate_tree now fails a non-ASCII-fixture test driven through the whole pipeline, and the permission test is a rejected/accepted twin set that kills all four mutants. Wave 2 (doc-rigor 0 blocking, ponytail-review 1 blocking) resurrected a wave-1 finding that had been DECLINED and proved the decline wrong: git archive always records 0664/0775 and tar --no-same-permissions masks with the AMBIENT umask, so at umask 002 or 000 the group-write bit survives and materialization rejects its own frozen base — data-free error, every retry identical, passing under systemd's 0022 and failing on a developer shell. Fixed by pinning the child's umask in pre_exec so extracted modes depend on the archive rather than the caller's shell; verified passing at umask 022, 002 and 000, and the mutation (child umask 002) fails. Implemented on task/ravel-amn.4 (stacked on task/ravel-amn.2), PR to follow. Candidate delta validation plus deterministic Git candidate construction in src/materialize.rs, returning a typed ConstructedCandidate. Design: spec-pipeline then two sign-off lanes, both SIGN OFF WITH CONDITIONS, whose seven amendments A1-A7 overturned THREE of the spec's ten resolved decisions. A1: the spec asserted twice that the transport has no deletion representation; probe showed git update-index --index-info DELETES tracked base entries on a directory/file conflict while write-tree returns 0, so a candidate writing a blob at tracked path src/export, or a child under tracked blob src/main.rs, makes contract.md's own target file src/export/tests.rs vanish from the candidate commit and the evaluator report PASS — the same harm class as e06-amn1-overlay-freshness. Recorded as e06-amn4-df-conflict-deletion. A2: the spec's path-validation-before-scope ordering rejected every candidate whose build SUCCEEDED, because cargo uplifts binaries by hard-linking so st_nlink>1 files always exist under target/ and /work/out is both HOME and the target dir; runtime.md:207-209 applies the predicate to entries of a VALIDATED delta, so scope-first pruning is frozen-conformant, with symlinked directories rejected rather than followed. A3: the spec's pre-commit grants::intake retest was guaranteed to return StaleAuthority for every real run (must_stop fires below a 5s margin on a 30s lease; evaluators take minutes), so a fully validated digested delta would be discarded 100 percent of the time; the caller must now supply an authority renewed AFTER the run, and Unavailable maps to a distinct retryable category instead of the permanent failure. A4: both lanes independently found the python collision-key protocol deadlocks at this bead's own limits (~720KB each way against a 65536-byte pipe, no timeout anywhere, so the RUNNER hangs) — fixed with read-to-EOF discipline plus count and per-index correspondence checks. A5: the Unicode version assertion moved to host preflight with a host category, because runtime.md:228-232 makes the 19 vectors the operative check and the version merely recorded, and a host defect must not record as a candidate rejection. A6: e06-effect-gate-taxonomy amended with entry 6 — local candidate object construction is EXCLUDED BY RULING (content-addressed objects into a local database, no ref updated, bounded by a fresh ownership retest rather than a grant action), leaving the code host as the only GENUINELY ABSENT effect. Review wave 1 (rust-code-reviewer 1 blocking, security-reviewer 1 blocking, invariant-test-review 2 blocking, less-code 0) then wave 2 (ponytail-review 0 blocking, doc-rigor 1 blocking). Four blocking findings, all fixed with mutation proofs: (i) two lanes INDEPENDENTLY bypassed the A1 fix, because the D/F guard tested only ADJACENT sorted keys and every allowed byte below 0x2F sorts between a parent and its children, so one ordinary in-scope sibling such as src/export.rs hid the conflict — replaced with a prefix-set test over all keys in collision-key space, with the bypass shape as a regression test; (ii) the ownership retest was deletable AND reorderable with a green suite and its retryability assertion was a tautology (two distinct fieldless variants of a derived-Eq enum can never compare equal) — the ordering is now COMPILE-ENFORCED by a private ZST OwnershipRetested that commit_candidate_tree requires, so moving the retest after the commit is error[E0425], matching amn.1's Reaped and amn.2's FabricatedFixture idiom; (iii) the index union-count guard had no test reaching it, only a direct call with a literal expected count — now driven through build_candidate_tree so placement and computed count are both observed; (iv) doc-rigor disproved half of a comment I had briefed: git commit-tree never consults commit.gpgsign, so --no-gpg-sign prevents nothing there and is precautionary, not load-bearing. ALSO CLOSED: amn.1 residual R11 in full — LaunchPaths is private, TrustedEvaluatorLaunch::new takes &MaterializedBase and CandidateLaunch::new takes &ConstructedCandidate, so trusted-base and candidate provenance are both compiler-enforced. Implemented on task/ravel-amn.6 (stacked on task/ravel-amn.4), PR to follow. Thin candidate bundle relative to the exact base, admitted into authoritative history through the EXISTING canonical scoped-v2 artifact_reference event, plus reconstruction and verification proven in a genuinely separate OS process. Design: spec-pipeline then two sign-off lanes, both SIGN OFF WITH CONDITIONS with seven probe-backed blocking objections, folded in as amendments A1-A7. ARTIFACT-RECORD CONTRACT (folded from ravel-6pv): verified that ravel-85q.2 already landed the canonical type (ArtifactKind at src/scope.rs:502, ArtifactReferencePayload at :553, ArtifactReferenceEvent at :649, ARTIFACT_REFERENCE_PAYLOAD_TYPE at :34), so this bead EXTENDS it with exactly one variant CandidateBundle / candidate_bundle / application/vnd.ravel.candidate-bundle+cbor and forks nothing; WireArtifactReferencePayload unchanged; malformed, unpublished, unsupported and wrong-scope references fail before the head advances with a negative test per class; frozen v1 conversion and tests/wire.rs fixtures unchanged. THE TWO FINDINGS THAT MATTERED MOST, both about the epic's own end-to-end proof: (1) e06-amn6-vacuous-child-proof — the spec required only that the child process exit successfully, but libtest EXITS 0 when its --exact filter matches nothing (probe: 'running 0 tests / test result: ok. 0 passed ... 1 filtered out', EXIT=0), so a renamed, mistyped, moved or cfg-gated-out child test would have made the entire epic's end-to-end proof pass while reconstructing NOTHING, silently and permanently; the repo already had the correct pattern at src/db/worker.rs:1311-1315 and the spec dropped it. Fixed by asserting the child's stdout contains both its own success marker RAVEL_CANDIDATE_RECONSTRUCTED and libtest's 'test result: ok. 1 passed;'. Mutation verified by the orchestrator: pointing the child at a non-existent test name now fails the parent with 'assertion failed: stdout.contains(RAVEL_CANDIDATE_RECONSTRUCTED)'. (2) Process separation alone proved nothing about provenance — the spec passed the expected digest by argv from a temp file while a separate in-process test covered publish plus append, so nothing tied the digest the child verified to the digest inside the committed event; the parent now publishes through the store, appends the artifact-reference event, asserts the head advanced by exactly one sequence, and hands the child the digest READ BACK OUT of the decoded event payload. The authority window bit for the FOURTH consecutive bead: the publication chain had no deadline and no clock re-read, and into_parent(now_ms) reuses the caller's now_ms so must_stop evaluated at the START instant while the head CAS is fenced on the parent rather than on liveness, meaning an unbounded chain could advance authoritative history under a LAPSED lease (residual R7 becoming durable); fixed by adopting grants::issue's landed discipline verbatim — precheck must_stop/namespace/scope/active-plan, one deadline = remaining_term_ms - STOP_MARGIN_MS, timeout_at on every await, elapsed charged before into_parent — and documenting that the authority must be renewed after construction. git fsck --strict would have REJECTED valid bundles: the pilot base is fetched --depth=1, and strict connectivity only passes when the destination carries the identical shallow boundary (probe: fsck exit=2 without the shallow marker, exit=0 with it), so fail-closed had been inverted into a false negative on the happy path; reconstruction now runs against a MaterializedBase produced by materialize(), i.e. the production shape, not a non-shallow local fixture that would have passed on the easy shape. Epic complete. All four acceptance criteria met across five stacked PRs, each mapped to the code and tests that prove it.

AC1 'Candidate processes have bounded resources, no ambient credentials, no network, and reap-safe cleanup' — ravel-amn.1 (PR #65). The frozen E01 bwrap runner reproduces runtime.md section 3.1 token-for-token: RLIMIT_AS 8 GiB, NPROC 512, CPU 900s, NOFILE 4096, wall clock 1800s with SIGKILL after 60, /tmp 2 GiB, an 8 GiB size-capped overlay, and independent 10 MiB stdout/stderr caps. Proof: 7 Linux host tests run and pass on the pilot host, including exact_environment_and_mount_visibility (ambient canaries incl. a credential-shaped one appear only when --clearenv is removed), network_and_unrelated_host_paths_are_unavailable, and every_termination_path_reaps_the_direct_child_and_descendants across normal exit, crash, in-sandbox timeout, cancellation and both output-overflow paths. Quiescence is the direct-child reap and nothing else, with Drop-backed teardown gated on a Reaped witness.

AC2 'Every candidate starts from the exact trusted Git base' — ravel-amn.2 (PR #66). materialize() verifies the frozen commit, the frozen tree, AND the sha256 of git archive output, extracting only after that digest matches. The fetch is bare, from an empty template, with cleared environment, system and global config disabled, core.hooksPath=/dev/null and no checkout; the tree parser rejects non-blob types, modes other than 100644/100755, and .gitmodules/.gitattributes/.cargo/config* at any depth, so repository-supplied hooks, filters and attributes never act. MaterializedBase has no public path accessor and LaunchPaths requires it, so a raw path cannot stand in for the trusted base.

AC3 'Only an allowed filesystem delta becomes an immutable Git candidate' — ravel-amn.4 (PR #67). Scope-pruned traversal admits only build.rs and src/**, rejects symlinked directories rather than walking them, and holds accepted entries to 2000 files / 1 MiB each / 32 MiB total / 180 path bytes / 10 components. The accepted bytes are digested before any Git write. The commit is deterministic (fixed author and committer identity and dates, cleared environment, no config discovery). Candidate identity binds base commit, delta digest, plan digest, work revision and attempt, each pinned by a test that changes it. The ownership retest before commit-tree is compile-enforced by a ZST witness.

AC4 'A second worker reconstructs and verifies the same candidate from its bundle' — ravel-amn.6 (PR #68). committed_candidate_event_reconstructs_in_a_fresh_process publishes the bundle, appends the canonical artifact_reference event, asserts the head advanced by one sequence, reads the digest back OUT of the decoded event payload, then spawns a separate OS process with env_clear() and argv-only inputs which materializes its own production-shaped shallow base and reconstructs the candidate, verifying commit, tree, base and bundle digests. The parent asserts the child's own success marker AND libtest's '1 passed' line, because a child that merely exits zero proves nothing. Missing, extra, corrupt and mismatched objects each fail closed with a test.
